regulatory.reference: K083033 (Vitoss, 2008-11-06); K103173 (Vitoss BA BiModal, 2011-02-07); K153608 (BiModal foam strip, 2016-02-12); K163621 (Vitoss BA Injectable, 2017-05-02); K242280 (BiModal foam strip, 2024-08-29); K261008 (BiModal family, 2026-04-24); applicant Orthovita / Stryker Spine; K102545 is a special 510(k) for a Vitoss formulation
on_label_indications: resorbable bone void filler for voids or gaps not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure in the extremities, pelvis and posterolateral spine, surgically created or from traumatic injury; may be combined with autograft or bone marrow aspirate (class labeling; the 2024 PDF could not be text-extracted)

applications.evidence_summary: Class evidence only: granular beta-TCP added nothing to angle-stable plating in a 39-patient RCT (Jakubietz 2011, PMID:21600042). No Vitoss-specific wrist trial found.
applications.caveats: Negative class-level result.

applications.evidence_summary: Synthetic void fill for the metaphyseal defect is described in the augmentation literature (Biermann 2019) without Vitoss-specific outcomes.
applications.caveats: No product data.

evidence.title: The use of beta-tricalcium phosphate bone graft substitute in dorsally plated, comminuted distal radius fractures
evidence.finding: No advantage of granular beta-TCP with angle-stable plating.

bd.reimbursement: Packaged into the procedure payment.
bd.notes: The 2024 clearance naming a 'BBTrauma' SKU signals Stryker is re-packaging the spine ceramic for its trauma bag; expect it to be bundled with plate contracts rather than sold on evidence.

products.catalog_status_2026: Stryker's US trauma-and-extremities bone grafting catalog page (read 2026-10-22) lists AlloFiber, AlloMatrix, Augment, BIO4, DBM, FusionFlex, HydroSet XT, Ignite, OsteoSet, Pro-Dense, Pro-Dense LoVisc, Pro-Stim, Tensix, Vitoss, Vitoss BA, Vitoss BA2X and Vitoss BBTrauma as current products.

products.name: Bioactive glass granules and putties (Bonalive S53P4; NovaBone 45S5 putty; Fibergraft BG)
products.company: Bonalive Biomaterials (Turku, Finland); NovaBone Products (Alachua, FL; Isto Biologics since August 2026); Prosidyan (Fibergraft)
products.ownership_history: BonAlive granules cleared via Vivoxid in 2007-2008 (K071199), re-cleared to Bonalive Biomaterials 2019 (K191274) and as 'Bonalive Orthopedics granules' 2023 (K231528). NovaBone putty cleared 2006-2024 (K060728 to K240404). Fibergraft BG morsels/putty/matrix cleared 2014-2025 (K141956 to K253147).
products.composition: S53P4 (53% SiO2) or 45S5 silicate glass; S53P4 raises local pH and osmotic pressure, which is the basis of its antibacterial claim in Europe.

regulatory.reference: K231528 (Bonalive, 2023-07-11); K240404 (NovaBone, 2024-03-05); K253147 (Fibergraft, 2025-10-22); Bonalive 510(k)s in openFDA: K070055 and K071199 (2007-2008, applicant Vivoxid), K191274 (2019-08-07), K231528 (Bonalive Orthopedics granules, 2023-07-11, adults and pediatric patients 6 years and older, extremities and pelvis), K253883 (Bonalive Maxillofacial, 2026-05-14)
on_label_indications: bone void filler for voids or gaps not intrinsic to the stability of the bony structure (extremities, pelvis, posterolateral spine); US labels carry no antibacterial or osteomyelitis indication (class labeling; PDFs not text-extracted)

applications.evidence_summary: Multinational registry of 116 chronic osteomyelitis patients treated with S53P4 as a one-stage dead-space filler without local antibiotics in 85%: cure in 104 of 116 (90%) at median 31 months, sites mainly tibia, femur and calcaneus (Lindfors 2017, PMID:28050878). The antibacterial use is off-label in the US.
applications.caveats: Registry without control; upper-extremity cases rare; US label is void-fill only.

applications.evidence_summary: Bioactive glass was listed among cleared wrist void fillers in 1999 (Ladd 1999, PMID:10504355) but no clinical wrist outcome series was found.
applications.caveats: No data.

evidence.title: Antibacterial bioactive glass, S53P4, for chronic bone infections - a multinational study
evidence.finding: 90% cure rate as a one-stage treatment in chronic osteomyelitis.

evidence.title: Bioactive glass S53P4 as bone graft substitute in treatment of osteomyelitis
evidence.finding: 9 of 11 healed without recurrence; lower extremity and spine.

bd.reimbursement: Packaged into the procedure payment.
bd.notes: Bonalive's 2023 US re-entry and Fibergraft's 2025 clearance show the category is active, but every US pitch has to avoid the European antibacterial claim; that gap is exactly what Cerament G's De Novo label fills.

products.name: Teriparatide (Forteo and generics/biosimilars) as a fracture-healing adjunct
products.company: Eli Lilly (Forteo); multiple generic and 505(b)(2) teriparatide products since 2019-2023
products.ownership_history: FDA-approved 2002 for osteoporosis; the fracture-healing use is off-label. Lilly sponsored the only distal radius RCT (NCT00190944).
products.composition: Recombinant PTH(1-34), 20 micrograms subcutaneously daily.

regulatory.reference: NDA 021318 (Drugs@FDA: NDA, not a BLA) (Forteo); fracture healing is not a labeled indication
on_label_indications: treatment of postmenopausal women with osteoporosis at high risk for fracture; increase of bone mass in men with primary or hypogonadal osteoporosis at high risk; glucocorticoid-induced osteoporosis (not fracture healing)

applications.evidence_summary: Lilly-sponsored double-blind RCT of 102 postmenopausal women with non-operated distal radius fractures: median time to cortical bridging 9.1 weeks placebo, 7.4 weeks with 20 micrograms, 8.8 weeks with 40 micrograms; the prespecified primary comparison (40 micrograms vs placebo) was not significant (p=0.52) and the 20-microgram benefit was post hoc (Aspenberg 2010, PMID:19594305; NCT00190944). A blinded callus-quality substudy favored teriparatide (PMID:20367417). Pooled across 5 RCTs (n=380) teriparatide did not shorten radiographic healing (Shi 2016, PMID:27997614).
applications.caveats: Failed primary endpoint; sponsor-funded; surrogate radiographic outcome; cost and daily injection. A Chinese weekly-teriparatide RCT (NCT04473989, n=80) has unknown status.

evidence.title: Teriparatide for acceleration of fracture repair in humans: a prospective, randomized, double-blind study of 102 postmenopausal women with distal radial fractures
evidence.finding: Primary 40-microgram comparison not significant; post hoc 20-microgram group bridged 1.7 weeks earlier.

evidence.title: Effectiveness of teriparatide on fracture healing: a systematic review and meta-analysis
evidence.finding: No significant effect on time to radiographic healing, healing rate or pain; function improved.

bd.reimbursement: Pharmacy benefit (Part D) for the osteoporosis indication; off-label fracture-healing use is not reimbursed as such and is prescribed, not sold by device reps.
bd.notes: Relevant to a device BD person only as the pharmacologic comparator surgeons mention, and as the osteoporosis-treatment gap that fragility fractures of the wrist and shoulder expose.

products.name: REGENETEN Bioinductive Implant
products.company: Smith+Nephew (Endoscopy division, Andover MA)
products.ownership_history: Developed by Rotation Medical (Plymouth, MN; Collagen Tendon Sheet K112423 cleared 2011, K122048 2013, K140300 2014); Smith+Nephew agreed to acquire Rotation Medical on 2017-10-23 ($125 million upfront plus up to $85 million contingent) and completed the acquisition on 2017-12-06. Smith+Nephew clearances K222501 (2023-05-11) and K242631 (2024-11-26).
products.composition: Bioabsorbable, highly porous bovine type I collagen sheet fixed over the bursal surface of the tendon with staples; induces a layer of new tendon-like tissue.

on_label_indications: management and protection of tendon or extra-articular ligament injuries in which there has been no substantial loss of tendon or ligament tissue (bioinductivity demonstrated for tendon only); the delivery system is indicated for arthroscopic delivery (K242631)

applications.evidence_summary: Sponsor-run prospective cohort of 115 full-thickness tears augmented at repair: supraspinatus thickness increased 12.5% (medium) and 17.1% (large) and radiographic retear was 11.5% in medium tears at 2 years (Bushnell 2022, PMID:35788057). Partial-thickness isolated bioinductive repair (n=33) showed tissue fill-in in 95-100% (Schlegel 2021, PMID:33220413). The sponsor's RCT in large/massive tears (NCT04450342, n=119) was terminated for a 'sponsor decision not related to safety' and the posted primary endpoint shows 6-month retear 57.1% (95% CI 41-72) augmented vs 50.0% (34-66) repair alone. A 2026 multicenter revision-repair cohort reported 28.6% retear at 12 months (Delgado 2026, PMID:40939824). A 400-patient global registry (NCT06857084) and an investigator RCT (NCT05439850, n=78) are ongoing.
applications.caveats: The only randomized data are unfavorable and unpublished; cohort data are company-funded with MRI surrogate endpoints; terminated trial NCT03734536 (partial-thickness, n=168) also has no publication found.
applications.challenge: A hiring manager will ask why the pivotal-style RCT was stopped and whether the candidate has read the posted results.

evidence.title: Prospective multicenter RCT of ARCR augmented with REGENETEN vs ARCR alone in large or massive full-thickness tears
evidence.finding: Terminated; posted 6-month retear 57.14% augmented vs 50.00% control; no statistical analysis posted.

evidence.title: Two-year outcomes with a bioinductive collagen implant used in augmentation of arthroscopic repair of full-thickness rotator cuff tears
evidence.finding: Retear 11.5% in medium tears at 2 years; tendon thickness increased.

evidence.title: Isolated bioinductive repair of partial-thickness rotator cuff tears using a resorbable bovine collagen implant: two-year outcomes
evidence.finding: Clinically and statistically improved ASES and Constant scores; MRI tissue fill-in in 95-100%.

bd.reimbursement: Rotator cuff repair is an ASC/HOPD procedure; the implant is packaged into the facility payment with no separate device code; Smith+Nephew has pursued a Category III CPT add-on code for bioinductive augmentation (status unverified).
bd.notes: Sold by Smith+Nephew sports-medicine reps, the same people who carry the company's bone-void and soft-tissue biologics; the commercial case rests on implant volume (tens of thousands per year, company claim) rather than randomized outcomes.

products.name: Acellular human dermal allograft patches for rotator cuff augmentation (GraftJacket, ArthroFlex, others)
products.company: GraftJacket: LifeCell/Allergan-processed, marketed by Wright Medical, now Stryker (orthopaedic rights; unverified); ArthroFlex: LifeNet Health, distributed by Arthrex
products.ownership_history: GraftJacket (Wright Medical, 2002 onward) moved to Stryker with the 2020 Wright acquisition; ArthroFlex launched by Arthrex/LifeNet around 2011 (dates from memory, unverified).
products.composition: Decellularized human dermis, 1-2 mm thick, sutured over or bridging the repaired cuff; regulated as a 361 HCT/P (no openFDA 510(k) record found for either brand).

regulatory.reference: No premarket number
on_label_indications: none; 361 tissue used at surgeon discretion for tendon augmentation or superior capsular reconstruction

applications.evidence_summary: Multicenter RCT of 42 patients with 2-tendon tears >3 cm: GraftJacket augmentation improved ASES (98.9 vs 94.8) and Constant (91.9 vs 85.3) scores at 24 months with better MRI intact-repair rates (Barber 2012, PMID:21978432). Arthrex is running a 120-patient randomized post-market study of dermal allograft augmentation in large/massive tears (NCT05981833, 2023-2025, status unknown).
applications.caveats: Single small RCT, industry-supported; most other data are superior capsular reconstruction series rather than augmentation.

evidence.title: A prospective, randomized evaluation of acellular human dermal matrix augmentation for arthroscopic rotator cuff repair
evidence.finding: Statistically better ASES and Constant scores with augmentation at mean 24 months.

products.name: Rotium Bioresorbable Wick
products.company: Atreon Orthopedics (Columbus, OH; 510(k) applicant Nanofiber Solutions, LLC)
products.ownership_history: Nanofiber Solutions spun out Atreon Orthopedics to commercialize Rotium; clearances K183236 (2019-03-11), K201414 (2020), K231641 (2023), K250021 (2025-02-27, new product code OWW).
products.composition: Electrospun bioresorbable synthetic nanofiber scaffold placed as an interpositional wick between the tendon and the greater tuberosity footprint during repair.

regulatory.reference: K250021 (Rotium; Nanofiber Solutions, LLC; decision 2025-02-27; 21 CFR 878.3300 surgical mesh, product code OWW, Class II); earlier Rotium Bioresorbable Wick K183236 (2019-03-11), K201414 (2020-06-25), K231641 (2023-07-05; product code MAI)
on_label_indications: Management and protection of tendon injuries without substantial loss of tendon tissue in patients requiring surgical intervention (K250021 Indications for Use; this is not a rotator-cuff-reinforcement or suture-augmentation indication)

applications.evidence_summary: Technique papers only (Beleckas 2023, PMID:36814979; Mousad 2025, PMID:40656718); a planned ultrasound-healing RCT was withdrawn with zero enrollment (NCT04361266).
applications.caveats: No clinical outcome data.

evidence.title: Bioaugmentation of rotator cuff repair with an interpositional nanofiber scaffold
evidence.finding: Surgical technique description; no outcomes.

pipeline.expected_milestone: No registered outcome trial active; next milestone is any comparative clinical series

bd.reimbursement: Packaged into the procedure payment.
bd.notes: Start-up in a category dominated by Smith+Nephew and Arthrex; included as the 'emerging' example in the rotator cuff adjacent note.

products.challenge: K250021 is a tendon-injury management/protection indication; any rotator-cuff augmentation claim is outside the cleared wording.
